plan: Given the private value of $31, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly below this value to maximize potential profit while minimizing loss if I win. Bidding exactly my value risks zero profit if I win. Rational bidders will also aim to bid slightly below their values. A bid of $30.9 balances competitiveness and potential profit.

Given my private value of $37, I should bid slightly below my value to maximize profit if I win. Rational bidders will bid up to their value. I aim to win by bidding just above the expected value of other bids. Assuming values are uniformly distributed, the average value is $24.5. To outbid others, I will bid slightly higher, considering the risk of overbidding and reducing profit. I'll bid $30 to balance winning chances and profit potential.

Given my private value of $11, I should bid slightly below it to maximize potential profit while minimizing the risk of overbidding. The optimal strategy in a sealed-bid auction is to bid less than my value to ensure a positive payoff if I win. Since all bidders are rational and know the value range, I will bid $10, slightly under my value, to outbid low bids but avoid paying more than my value.
